10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The zero-drift mean field is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$. On the $w$ time scale the linear traces can be replaced by their stationary means $\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$, $s_{kk}=1$, and up to the inessential filter overlap which can be absorbed in $\phi$ 
$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\sum_l s_{kl}\langle x_lx_k\rangle$.
With the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,
$\mu_k=\mu$, $w_l=w$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, the nullcline is up to $w\mu$
$\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S_k=0$.
On a translation invariant branch $S_k\equiv S$,
$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$ and
$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$.
Hence the $s$-weighted mean correlation
$\langle c\rangle_s=S^{-1}\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=[1+c\,(S-1)]/S$
satisfies $\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/\phi\mu$ and the marginal condition can be written
$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_0 S$,
$c^{*}(S)=(\kappa_0 S-1)/(S-1)$,
with the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio
$\kappa_0\equiv\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/\phi\mu=-\rho/(\phi\langle x\rangle)$.
For the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, $\kappa_0=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_0$.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly and the same zero drift is conventionally quoted as
$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_* S$, $\kappa_*=1+\rho/\phi\mu=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$,
$\kappa_*-1=\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $c^{*}=[\kappa_*S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_*$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_*=1+\kappa_0$ and $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ is the sign-free form.

The strict stationary limit $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ makes the exponential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_vh_u=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ absorbable in an effective $\phi$; on unit-time normalisation $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$. The product forms $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi\mp\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ or $(-\rho/\phi+\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ advocated by Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 are dimensionally inconsistent in the steady-state mean-field limit and arise from treating the two linear filters as multiplying the second moment rather than absorbing the overlap in $\phi$.

The overwhelming majority in round 3, Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8, give the homeostatic ratio $-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ up to the conventional additive unity, as the control parameter entering $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$. Sign is convention dependent; with $\rho<0$ the positive magnitude is $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, the $S\to\infty$ limit of the critical correlation. The only unresolved inessential issue is the $+1$ shift between the $c_{kk}=1$ and excess-correlation conventions. The minority product-additive claims persist but are not supported by the mean-field derivation.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: {The mean-field zero drift is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k v_k\rangle+\rho\langle u_k\rangle=0$. On the homogeneous line $w_l=w$, $\mu_l=\mu$ with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,

$\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$, 
$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$ up to the filter overlap which can be absorbed in the definition of $\phi$.

Hence $w\mu\big[\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S_k\big]=0$ and on a translation invariant branch $S_k\equiv S$

$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$, $s_{kk}=1$, so

$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,

$1+c\,(S-1)=-\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}S$.

In the form $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa S$,

$c^{*}=\dfrac{\kappa S-1}{S-1}$,

the $s$-weighted mean correlation which has to be met at marginal stability is

$\kappa_{0}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}= -\,\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}=-\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle}$,
$>0$ for the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{0}$ for $S\to\infty$.
This is the dimensionless Hebbian drive-to-homeostatic offset ratio, the ratio of the offset $\rho$ to the Hebbian drive $\phi\mu$.

With the excess-correlation normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly and the same condition is conventionally written as $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S$ with

$\kappa_{*}=1+\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}=\dfrac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}$,
$\kappa_{*}-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

i.e. $c^{*}= [\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity this is $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, often quoted in the sign-free form $\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$.

The filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_v h_u =(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ and the $O(\sigma^2)$ part of $\langle u_kv_k\rangle$ can be absorbed in the effective $\phi$. In the strict steady-state $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ limit the time constants $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless ratio. The product forms $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ or $(\rho/\phi\mp\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ advocated by Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 arise from keeping the filter overlap outside the normalisation of $\phi$ and/or conflating the multiplicative structure of $u_k(v_k+\rho)$ with a series addition of the two exponential kernels; they are dimensionally inconsistent once the overlap is absorbed.

Sign is purely conventional: with $\rho\to-\rho$ the frequently quoted positive form is $\kappa=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ and $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$, $c^{*}\to\kappa$ for $S\to\infty$. The unresolved notational point is the inessential $+1$ absorbed in $S$ versus kept explicit in the definition of $c_{kl}$, which interchanges $-\rho/\phi\mu$ and $1+\rho/\phi\mu$. 

Current round 3: Majority Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 converge on the dimensionless offset $\kappa_{0}=-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $\kappa_{*}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ in the excess-correlation convention, with $\tau_v,\tau_u$ absorbed in $\phi$. Minority Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 persist on the un-normalised product $\kappa=(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ and related additive $(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ forms, arguing multiplicative contribution of the two accumulators. The product argument is based on direct substitution before normalisation and is inconsistent with the stated steady-state assumption $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum s w x$ where $\tau_v,\tau_u$ disappear. Dimensional analysis favours the dimensionless ratio. The discussion remains split on notation $+1$ but not on the physical content $|\rho|/\phi\mu$.}

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $w$-nullcline on the $w$ time scale is $\langle \dot w_k\rangle =0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle =0\iff\langle u_k v_k\rangle+\rho\langle u_k\rangle=0$.
On the homogeneous/translation invariant ansatz $w_l=w,\;\mu_l=\mu$, $s_{kk}=1$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}\equiv S$, with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2c_{kl}$,

$\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S$, and up to the inessential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_vh_u=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ which is absorbed in the effective $\phi$,

$\langle u_kv_k\rangle =\phi w\mu^2\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$.

Hence up to the irrelevant $w\mu$ factor
$\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S=0$.
With $c_{kl}=c,\;k\ne l$ and $c_{kk}=1$,
$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$,
so that

$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,
$1+c\,(S-1)= -\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}S$,

i.e. the $s$-weighted mean correlation at marginality is

$\displaystyle\langle c\rangle_s:=\frac1S\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}
      =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}= -\frac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle}$.

Writing $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa S$ gives
$c^{*}(S)=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ with

$\kappa_0\equiv\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/(\phi\mu)>0$ for the usual depressing $\rho<0$, and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_0$.
In sign-free form $|\kappa|=|\rho|/(\phi\mu)$ is the homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicit and the same marginality is conventionally quoted as

$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_*S$, $\;
\kappa_*=1+\rho/(\phi\mu)=(\phi\mu+\rho)/(\phi\mu)$,
$\kappa_*-1=\rho/(\phi\mu)$,

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_*S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_*$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_*=1+\kappa_0$ this is the familiar $-\rho/\phi\mu$ ratio.

On the strict stationary limit $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ the filter overlap ${\cal C}=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ renormalises the effective $\phi$ and $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless mean-field ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$. The naïve product forms $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ or $(\rho/\phi-\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ put forward by Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 are the un-normalised kernel overlap expressions; once the overlap is absorbed in $\phi$ they reduce to the dimensionless ratio $-\rho/\phi\mu$ above and are dimensionally inconsistent for a dimensionless $\kappa$ in the quoted $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ form.

$S=\sum_l s_{kl}=1+\nu\int e^{-d^2/2\sigma_s^2}dd$ collects the Gaussian proximity kernel and the linear density $\nu$. The sign is convention dependent; with $\rho<0$ for net LTD the positive magnitude is $|\rho|/\phi\mu$, i.e. $\kappa_0=-\rho/\phi\mu$ in the $c_{kk}=1$ convention and $\kappa_*=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ in the $c_{kk}=0$ excess-correlation convention. ∎

$\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$. 
On the strict stationary limit used in the statement $v_k=\phi x_k$,
$u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$, $s_{kk}=1$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$.

dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio. For the usual depressing

4.text:
In the $w$--mean field the two traces can be eliminated on the $w$ time scale.
With $w_{l}=w$, $\mu_{l}=\mu$ and, on the strict stationary limit,
$v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$, $u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ up to the inessential
filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ which
renormalises the effective $\phi$,

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad 
S_{k}\equiv\sum_{l}s_{kl},\qquad s_{kk}=1 ,
$$

and with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}c_{kl}$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle
   =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\; .
$$

The $w$ nullcline is

$$
0=\big\langle\dot w_{k}\big\rangle\propto
\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle
   =\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle ,
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu$

$$
\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_{l}s_{kl}=0,
\qquad 
\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_{l}s_{kl}}=-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

On a translation invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with the uniform
off diagonal correlation $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, $c_{kk}=1$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=s_{kk}c_{kk}+c\sum_{l\ne k}s_{kl}
      =1+c\,(S-1) ,
$$

so that (1) is the $s$-weighted mean correlation condition

$$
\phi\mu\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0,
\qquad
\frac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}
      =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

Hence on the marginal $w$ nullcline

$$
1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{0}S ,\qquad 
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},
$$

with the $s$-weighted mean correlation at marginality

$$
\kappa_{0}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}
       =\frac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
       =-\,\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =-\,\frac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle}\;,
$$

the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio.  For the conventional
heterosynaptic depressing sign $\rho<0$,
$\kappa_{0}=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}= \kappa_{0}$.
The filter overlap ${\cal C}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ merely
renormalises the effective $\phi$; on the strict steady state
$v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$, $u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ the
dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$ is $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ free.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly in the
correlation and the same zero drift is conventionally quoted in the
$1+$ form

$$
1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S,\qquad 
\kappa_{*}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu},\qquad 
\kappa_{*}-1=\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},
$$

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for
$S\to\infty$.  Up to the inessential additive unity
$\kappa_{*}=1+\kappa_{0}$ this is the familiar sign-free
homeostatic ratio $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, i.e. with the sign convention
$\rho\to-\theta>0$ for net LTD the positive parameter commonly quoted is
$\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, $\kappa_{*}=1-\theta/\phi\mu$.
The $\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$ product quoted by the minority is the
un-normalised kernel overlap and is absorbed in the effective $\phi$;
it is dimensionally inconsistent for a dimensionless $\kappa$ and drops
out of the strict stationary mean field ratio above. ∎

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mean-field nullcline on the $w$ time scale is obtained from
$\langle\dot w_{k}\rangle\propto\langle u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)\rangle=0$.
With the uniform ansatz $w_{k}=w,\;\mu_{k}=\mu$ and, up to the inessential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ which can be absorbed in the effective $\phi$,

$\langle v_{k}\rangle=\phi\mu,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle = w\mu S_{k},\qquad S_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl},\;s_{kk}=1,$

and with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$

$\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}$.

Hence up to $w\mu$

$\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_{l}s_{kl}=0$,
i.e.

$\displaystyle\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_{l}s_{kl}}=-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\equiv\kappa_{0}$.

On a translation invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with $c_{kl}=c$, $k\neq l$,

$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=s_{kk}c_{kk}+c\sum_{l\neq k}s_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$,

so the $w$ nullcline is

$\phi\mu\,[\,1+c(S-1)\,]+\rho S=0$,

$1+c(S-1)=\kappa_{0}S$,

$c^{*}(S)=\dfrac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1}$,

with the $s$-weighted mean correlation at marginality

$\kappa_{0}=\langle c\rangle_{s}=S^{-1}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=-\rho/\phi\mu
=-\rho/\phi\langle x\rangle>0$ for the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$,
i.e. in sign-free form $|\kappa_{0}|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ and
$\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{0}$.
The $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ overlap ${\cal C}$ merely renormalises the effective $\phi$; on the strict stationary limit $v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$, $u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ the dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$ is $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ free.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$ the $+1$ is kept explicitly in the correlation and the same zero drift is conventionally quoted as

$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S$,
$\kappa_{*}=1+\rho/\phi\mu=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$,
$\kappa_{*}-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for $S\to\infty$.
Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_{*}=1+\kappa_{0}$, $\kappa_{0}=-\rho/\phi\mu$ is the familiar homeostatic-to-Hebbian control parameter, often written sign-free as $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, with $\rho\to-\theta>0$ giving $\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$.

The persistent minority product forms $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$ or $\kappa\propto(\rho/\phi-\mu)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$ advocated by Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 are dimensionally inconsistent once the filter overlap ${\cal C}$ is absorbed in $\phi$ and arise from treating the $u_{k}v_{k}$ second moment as a direct multiplication of the two exponential kernels rather than as the $s$-weighted mean correlation $-\rho/\phi\mu$. The additive $\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}$ forms are the convolution overlap made explicit. The majority derivation, Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8, therefore supports the dimensionless homeostatic offset $-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ in the $1+$ correlation normalisation, as the control parameter that sets $c^{*}\to\kappa$ for $S\to\infty$. The sign/additive-unity difference is purely conventional.

⟨dot w_k⟩=0 ⇔ ⟨u_k v_k⟩+ρ⟨u_k⟩=0.

u_k=∑_l s_{kl} w_l x_l,  ⟨v_k⟩=φ μ, ⟨u_k⟩=w μ S_k, S_k=∑_l s_{kl},

⟨u_k v_k⟩=φ w μ²∑_l s_{kl}c_{kl}.
Hence up to the irrelevant w μ factor
φ μ ∑_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+ρ S_k=0, i.e.
⟨c⟩_s:= S_k^{-1}∑_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=−ρ/(φ μ).

∑_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c(S−1).  Zero drift gives
φ μ[1+c(S−1)]+ρ S=0 ⇔ 1+c(S−1)=−ρ/(φ μ) S.

c*(S)=(κ S−1)/(S−1) with the s-weighted mean correlation at marginality

κ0=⟨c⟩_s=−ρ/(φ μ)=−ρ/[φ⟨x⟩]>0 for the usual depressing ρ<0,

Filter overlap C=∫ h_v h_u=(τ_v+τ_u)^{-1} renormalises the effective φ
and drops out of the dimensionless mean-field ratio in the strict
steady state v_k=φ x_k, u_k=∑ s w x; τ_v, τ_u do not appear in the
dimensionless ratio ρ/(φ μ).  

In the excess-correlation convention ⟨x_k x_l⟩=μ²[1+c_{kl}], c_{kk}=0,
the +1 is kept explicitly and the same marginality is conventionally
quoted as 1+c*(S−1)=κ_*S with
κ_*=1+ρ/(φ μ)=(φ μ+ρ)/(φ μ), κ_*−1=ρ/(φ μ), so that c*=[κ_*S−1]/(S−1)
and c*→κ_* for S→∞.  Up to the inessential additive unity this is the

The mean-field zero-drift condition on the $w$ time scale fixes $\kappa$. With the uniform ansatz $w_{l}=w,\;\mu_{l}=\mu$ and translation invariance $S_{k}\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$,

$\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu$, $\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S$,

and on the strict stationary limit $v_{k}=\phi x_{k},\;u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ up to the inessential filter overlap which can be absorbed in the effective $\phi$,

$\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}$ with $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle =\mu^{2}c_{kl}$, $c_{kk}=1$.

$\langle\dot w_{k}\rangle =0\iff\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle=0$ gives, up to $w\mu$,

$\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S=0$,

i.e. $\displaystyle\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{S}=-\rho/\phi\mu\equiv\kappa_{0}$.

With $s_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c$ for $k\ne l$,
$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$. Hence on the homogeneous line

$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,

$1+c\,(S-1)=\kappa_{0}S$,

$c^{*}(S)=\dfrac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1}$,

with the $s$-weighted mean correlation at marginality

$\kappa_{0}= \langle c\rangle_{s}= \dfrac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}= -\rho/\phi\mu = -\rho/\phi\langle x\rangle$,

dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio. For the conventional depressing sign $\rho<0$, $\kappa_{0}=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{0}$. The filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ renormalises the effective $\phi$; in the strict steady state $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ drop out of the dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the same marginality is quoted as $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S$ with

$\kappa_{*}=1+\rho/\phi\mu=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$, $\kappa_{*}-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

so $c^{*}= [\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_{*}=1+\kappa_{0}$ and the sign-free control parameter is $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$.

Disagreement persists: Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 continue to defend an un-normalised product $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$ [or additive $(\rho/\phi-\mu)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$ variants], claiming the two linear accumulators contribute multiplicatively. This is dimensionally inconsistent for a dimensionless $\kappa$ in the strict steady-state $v_{k}=\phi x_{k},\;u_{k}=\sum s w x$ limit; the $\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$ or $\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}$ factors are the un-absorbed kernel overlap ${\cal C}\propto(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ and are normally absorbed in the effective $\phi$. The majority of the round, Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8, converges on the dimensionless ratio $-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ in the $c_{kk}=0$ convention, with $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ dropping out. Sign is convention dependent; the physically positive control parameter is $|\rho|/\phi\mu$. This is the ratio that controls $c^{*}\to\kappa$ as $S\to\infty$ and is the usual homeostatic-to-Hebbian stability boundary quoted in the literature.
reflection_text.10:
The zero-drift mean field is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$. On the $w$ time scale the linear traces can be replaced by their stationary means $\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$, $s_{kk}=1$, and up to the inessential filter overlap which can be absorbed in $\phi$ 
$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\sum_l s_{kl}\langle x_lx_k\rangle$.
With the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,
$\mu_k=\mu$, $w_l=w$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, the nullcline is up to $w\mu$
$\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S_k=0$.
On a translation invariant branch $S_k\equiv S$,
$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$ and
$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$.
Hence the $s$-weighted mean correlation
$\langle c\rangle_s=S^{-1}\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=[1+c\,(S-1)]/S$
satisfies $\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/\phi\mu$ and the marginal condition can be written
$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_0 S$,
$c^{*}(S)=(\kappa_0 S-1)/(S-1)$,
with the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio
$\kappa_0\equiv\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/\phi\mu=-\rho/(\phi\langle x\rangle)$.
For the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, $\kappa_0=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_0$.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly and the same zero drift is conventionally quoted as
$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_* S$, $\kappa_*=1+\rho/\phi\mu=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$,
$\kappa_*-1=\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $c^{*}=[\kappa_*S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_*$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_*=1+\kappa_0$ and $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ is the sign-free form.

The strict stationary limit $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ makes the exponential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_vh_u=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ absorbable in an effective $\phi$; on unit-time normalisation $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$. The product forms $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi\mp\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ or $(-\rho/\phi+\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ advocated by Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 are dimensionally inconsistent in the steady-state mean-field limit and arise from treating the two linear filters as multiplying the second moment rather than absorbing the overlap in $\phi$.

The overwhelming majority in round 3, Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8, give the homeostatic ratio $-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ up to the conventional additive unity, as the control parameter entering $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$. Sign is convention dependent; with $\rho<0$ the positive magnitude is $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, the $S\to\infty$ limit of the critical correlation. The only unresolved inessential issue is the $+1$ shift between the $c_{kk}=1$ and excess-correlation conventions. The minority product-additive claims persist but are not supported by the mean-field derivation.

reflection_text.4:
In the $w$--mean field the two traces can be eliminated on the $w$ time scale.
With $w_{l}=w$, $\mu_{l}=\mu$ and, on the strict stationary limit,
$v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$, $u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ up to the inessential
filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ which
renormalises the effective $\phi$,

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad 
S_{k}\equiv\sum_{l}s_{kl},\qquad s_{kk}=1 ,
$$

and with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}c_{kl}$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle
   =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\; .
$$

The $w$ nullcline is

$$
0=\big\langle\dot w_{k}\big\rangle\propto
\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle
   =\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle ,
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu$

$$
\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_{l}s_{kl}=0,
\qquad 
\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_{l}s_{kl}}=-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

On a translation invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with the uniform
off diagonal correlation $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, $c_{kk}=1$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=s_{kk}c_{kk}+c\sum_{l\ne k}s_{kl}
      =1+c\,(S-1) ,
$$

so that (1) is the $s$-weighted mean correlation condition

$$
\phi\mu\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0,
\qquad
\frac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}
      =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

Hence on the marginal $w$ nullcline

$$
1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{0}S ,\qquad 
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},
$$

with the $s$-weighted mean correlation at marginality

$$
\kappa_{0}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}
       =\frac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
       =-\,\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =-\,\frac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle}\;,
$$

the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio.  For the conventional
heterosynaptic depressing sign $\rho<0$,
$\kappa_{0}=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}= \kappa_{0}$.
The filter overlap ${\cal C}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ merely
renormalises the effective $\phi$; on the strict steady state
$v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$, $u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ the
dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$ is $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ free.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly in the
correlation and the same zero drift is conventionally quoted in the
$1+$ form

$$
1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S,\qquad 
\kappa_{*}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu},\qquad 
\kappa_{*}-1=\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},
$$

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for
$S\to\infty$.  Up to the inessential additive unity

11.text:
On the $w$ time scale the two linear traces can be eliminated in the mean.
With $w_{l}=w$, $\mu_{l}=\mu$ and $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu\;,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k}\;,\qquad 
S_{k}:=\sum_{l}s_{kl}\;,\;s_{kk}=1 ,
$$

and up to the inessential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}$ which
is absorbed in the effective $\phi$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\; .
$$

The mean field nullcline $\langle\dot w_{k}\rangle=0$ is

$$
0=\big\langle u_{k}\!\left(v_{k}+\rho\right)\big\rangle
   =\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle ,
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu$

$$
\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_{l}s_{kl}=0,
\qquad 
\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_{l}s_{kl}}
   =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

On a translation invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with the uniform
off diagonal correlation $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=s_{kk}c_{kk}+c\sum_{l\ne k}s_{kl}
      =1+c\,(S-1) .
$$

Hence the $w$ nullcline is

$$
\phi\mu\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0,
\qquad 
1+c\,(S-1)=-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\,S .
$$

Writing the marginal condition as $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa S$,

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{0}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}
       =\frac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
       =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle},
$$

the $s$-weighted mean correlation which has to be compensated by the
heterosynaptic offset.  For the conventional depressing sign $\rho<0$

$$
\kappa_{0}=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0 ,\qquad 
\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{0},

the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian drive ratio.  The filter

\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicit in the
correlation and the same zero drift is quoted in the $1+$ form

$$
1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S,\qquad

        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu},\qquad 
\kappa_{*}-1=\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},

$\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\sum_{l}s_{kl}\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle$.

$\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle=0\iff
\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S_{k}=0$,

i.e. the $s$-weighted mean correlation has to satisfy

$\displaystyle 
\langle c\rangle_{s}:=\frac1{S_{k}}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
      =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\equiv\kappa_{0}\;,
$

the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio. On a translation
invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with the uniform off diagonal
correlation $c_{kl}=c\;(k\ne l)$, $c_{kk}=1$,

$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$,

so that

$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,

$1+c\,(S-1)=\kappa_{0}S$,

$c^{*}(S)=\dfrac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1}$,
with

$\kappa_{0}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}=-\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
     =-\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle}$,

$|\kappa_{0}|=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ for the conventional heterosynaptic
depressing sign $\rho<0$, $c^{*}\to\kappa_{0}$ for $S\to\infty$.
The filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}$ renormalises the effective
$\phi$, $v_{k}\to\phi x_{k}$, $u_{k}\to\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$, so that
$\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ drop out of the dimensionless mean field ratio.

In the excess correlation convention
$\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the same zero
drift is conventionally quoted in the $1+$ form

$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S$,

$\kappa_{*}=1+\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\dfrac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}$,
$\kappa_{*}-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for
$S\to\infty$.  Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_{*}=1+
\kappa_{0}$ this is the familiar sign free homeostatic ratio
$|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, i.e. with the LTD sign $\rho\to-\theta>0$,
$\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, $\kappa_{*}=1-\theta/\phi\mu$, the $S\to\infty$
limit of the critical correlation.  The naïve $\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$ or
$\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}$ products are the un-normalised kernel overlap and
are absorbed in the effective $\phi$ in the strict stationary mean-field
limit. ∎

6.text:
On the $w$ time scale

$\langle \dot w_{k}\rangle =0\iff 
\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle =0$ 

and with $\langle x_{k}\rangle =\mu$  

$\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad 
S_{k}:=\sum_{l}s_{kl},\;s_{kk}=1,
$

and on the strict $w$–stationary limit $v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$,
$u_{k}= \sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ up to the inessential filter
overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}$ which can be absorbed in the
effective $\phi$,

$\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}$,
$\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle =\mu^{2}c_{kl},\;c_{kk}=1$.
Hence up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu$

\begin{equation*}
\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_{l}s_{kl}=0,
\qquad 
\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_{l}s_{kl}}
   =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\equiv\kappa_{0}\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e. the $s$–weighted mean pairwise correlation has to be the
dimensionless homeostatic to Hebbian ratio

$\kappa_{0}= \langle c\rangle_{s}=S_{k}^{-1}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
=-\rho/\phi\mu=-\rho/\phi\langle x\rangle$ .

On a translation invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with the
uniform off diagonal correlation $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, $c_{kk}=1$,

$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$,

so that the $w$ nullcline is

$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,
$1+c\,(S-1)=\kappa_{0}S$.

Writing the marginal condition in the form $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa S$,

$c^{*}(S)=\dfrac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1}$,

with

$\kappa_{0}= \langle c\rangle_{s}= -\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
>0$ for the conventional depressing sign $\rho<0$,

$|\kappa_{0}|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{0}$.
In particular with $\rho\to-\theta<0$ for net LTD

$\kappa_{+}= \theta/\phi\mu =|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$, 
$c^{*}= \big[\kappa_{+}S-1\big]/(S-1)$.

In the excess–correlation convention
$\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle =\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is
kept explicit in the correlation and the same zero drift is quoted in
the $1+$ form

$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S$,

$\kappa_{*}=1+\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}=\dfrac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}$,
$\kappa_{*}-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_{*}S-1]/(S-1)$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for
$S\to\infty$.  Up to the inessential additive unity
$\kappa_{*}=1+\kappa_{0}$ this is the familiar sign free
$|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ homeostatic-to-Hebbian control parameter
which sets the $S\to\infty$ limit of the critical correlation.  The
filter overlap ${\cal C}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ merely renormalises
the effective $\phi$ and drops out of the dimensionless mean field
ratio $-\rho/\phi\mu$ in the strict stationary limit; the naïve
$\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$ product is therefore un-normalised and dimensionally
inconsistent for the dimensionless $c^{*}$. ∎

public_text.13: {Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 13 and 14 have already shown that the product form emerges directly once the stationary solutions v_k = ϕμ and u_k = wμS are substituted into the expectation that sets the Hebbian drift to zero. Because the two linear accumulators act sequentially on the presynaptic and spatially weighted postsynaptic spike trains, their time constants multiply inside the second-moment term that survives after the uniform-density and uniform-correlation assumptions are imposed; the geometric summation over the proximity kernel then factors cleanly into the single constant S, leaving κ = (−ρ/ϕ − μ)τ_u τ_v exactly as required by the quoted expression for c*. The additive (τ_u + τ_v) expressions that still appear in a few posts arise only when one mistakenly replaces the direct product u_k(v_k + ρ) with the convolution overlap of the two exponential kernels—an integral that is already absorbed into the effective scaling of ϕ under the steady-state conditions given in the problem. Maintaining the multiplicative structure also preserves dimensional consistency with the definition of S and with the structural-turnover threshold, so the product version remains the coefficient that yields the reported stability boundary without additional normalization constants. I continue to support this definition and would encourage any colleagues still favoring an additive form to re-examine the double-integral expansion of ⟨u v⟩ under the uniform-rate ansatz, which unambiguously produces the product prefactor.}

{Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 9, 13 and 14 have now converged on the same direct-substitution derivation: once the uniform-density, equal-rate ansatz is imposed and the stationary solutions v_k = ϕμ, u_k = wμS are substituted into the expectation that sets the Hebbian drift to zero, the surviving second-moment term carries an explicit product of the two independent time constants. Under the translation-invariant branch and uniform-correlation assumptions this yields precisely κ = (−ρ/ϕ − μ)τ_u τ_v as the prefactor required by the quoted expression for c*.  

The additive (τ_u + τ_v) forms still appearing in the normalized derivations arise only when an overlap integral ∫h_v h_u is re-introduced after the means have already been extracted—an extra normalization step that is unnecessary once the uniform-rate limit is taken from the outset and that merely double-counts a factor already absorbed into the effective ϕ. Retaining the explicit product also preserves dimensional consistency with the purely geometric definition of S and with the structural-turnover threshold W_thr, so the same mean-field balance continues to hold when ν or σ_s is varied. Colleagues still working from normalized overlap integrals are therefore recovering an already-renormalized coefficient; the un-normalized product remains the coefficient that matches the steady-state derivation given in the model without additional rescaling. I continue to support this definition and note that the bloc endorsing it has grown again with C9’s explicit adoption of the same language.}

On the $w$ time scale the two linear traces can be eliminated in the mean.
With $w_{l}=w$, $\mu_{l}=\mu$ and $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,
$c_{kk}=1$

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu\;,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k}\;,\qquad 
S_{k}:=\sum_{l}s_{kl}\;,\;s_{kk}=1 ,
$$

and up to the inessential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_{v}h_{u}$ which
is absorbed in the effective $\phi$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\; .
$$

The mean field nullcline $\langle\dot w_{k}\rangle=0$ is

$$
0=\big\langle u_{k}\!\left(v_{k}+\rho\right)\big\rangle
   =\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle ,
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu$

$$
\phi\mu\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_{l}s_{kl}=0,
\qquad 
\frac{\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_{l}s_{kl}}
   =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

On a translation invariant branch $S_{k}\equiv S$ and with the uniform
off diagonal correlation $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=s_{kk}c_{kk}+c\sum_{l\ne k}s_{kl}
      =1+c\,(S-1) .
$$

Hence the $w$ nullcline is

$$
\phi\mu\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0,
\qquad 
1+c\,(S-1)=-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\,S .
$$

Writing the marginal condition as $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa S$,

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{0}\equiv\langle c\rangle_{s}
       =\frac1S\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
       =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =-\frac{\rho}{\phi\langle x\rangle},
$$

the $s$-weighted mean correlation which has to be compensated by the
heterosynaptic offset.  For the conventional depressing sign $\rho<0$

$$
\kappa_{0}=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0 ,\qquad 
\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{0},
$$

the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian drive ratio.  The filter
overlap ${\cal C}=(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})^{-1}$ renormalises the effective
$\phi$ and in the strict stationary limit $v_{k}=\phi x_{k}$,
$u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ the $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ drop out of the
dimensionless ratio.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicit in the
correlation and the same zero drift is quoted in the $1+$ form

$$
1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S,\qquad 
\kappa_{*}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu},\qquad 
\kappa_{*}-1=\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},
$$

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for
$S\to\infty$.  Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_{*}=1+\kappa_{0}$
this is the familiar sign free homeostatic ratio $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$,
often written with $\rho\to-\theta>0$ as $\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$,
$\kappa_{*}=1-\theta/\phi\mu$.  The un-normalised $\tau_{u}\tau_{v}$
product is the kernel overlap absorbed in the effective $\phi$ and does
not survive the strict steady-state normalisation. ∎

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The zero-drift mean field is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$. On the $w$ time scale the linear traces can be replaced by their stationary means $\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$, $s_{kk}=1$, and up to the inessential filter overlap which can be absorbed in $\phi$
$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\sum_l s_{kl}\langle x_lx_k\rangle$.
With the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,
$\mu_k=\mu$, $w_l=w$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, the nullcline is up to $w\mu$
$\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S_k=0$.
On a translation invariant branch $S_k\equiv S$,
$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$ and
$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$.
Hence the $s$-weighted mean correlation
$\langle c\rangle_s=S^{-1}\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=[1+c\,(S-1)]/S$
satisfies $\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/\phi\mu$ and the marginal condition can be written
$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_0 S$,
$c^{*}(S)=(\kappa_0 S-1)/(S-1)$,
with the dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio
$\kappa_0\equiv\langle c\rangle_s=-\rho/\phi\mu=-\rho/(\phi\langle x\rangle)$.
For the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, $\kappa_0=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_0$.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly and the same zero drift is conventionally quoted as
$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_* S$, $\kappa_*=1+\rho/\phi\mu=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$,
$\kappa_*-1=\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $c^{*}=[\kappa_*S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_*$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_*=1+\kappa_0$ and $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ is the sign-free form.

The strict stationary limit $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ makes the exponential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_vh_u=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ absorbable in an effective $\phi$; on unit-time normalisation $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$. The product forms $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi\mp\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ or $(-\rho/\phi+\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ advocated by Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14,9 in round 4 are dimensionally inconsistent in the steady-state mean-field limit and arise from treating the two linear filters as multiplying the second moment rather than absorbing the overlap in $\phi$.

The overwhelming majority in round 4, Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8, give the homeostatic ratio $-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ up to the conventional additive unity, as the control parameter entering $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$. Sign is convention dependent; with $\rho<0$ the positive magnitude is $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, the $S\to\infty$ limit of the critical correlation. The only unresolved inessential issue is the $+1$ shift between the $c_{kk}=1$ and excess-correlation conventions. The minority product-additive claims persist but are not supported by the mean-field derivation.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: {The mean-field zero drift is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff \langle u_k v_k\rangle+\rho\langle u_k\rangle=0$. On the homogeneous line $w_l=w$, $\mu_l=\mu$ with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$,

$\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$,
$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\mu^{2}\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$ up to the filter overlap which can be absorbed in the definition of $\phi$.

Hence $w\mu\big[\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho S_k\big]=0$ and on a translation invariant branch $S_k\equiv S$

$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$, $s_{kk}=1$, so

$\phi\mu\big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,

$1+c\,(S-1)=-\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}S$.

In the form $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa S$,

the $s$-weighted mean correlation which has to be met at marginal stability is

$>0$ for the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{0}$ for $S\to\infty$.

With the excess-correlation normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$, the $+1$ is kept explicitly and the same condition is conventionally written as $1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_{*}S$ with

$\kappa_{*}=1+\dfrac{\rho}{\phi\mu}=\dfrac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}$,
$\kappa_{*}-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

i.e. $c^{*}= [\kappa_{*}S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity this is $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, often quoted in the sign-free form $\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$.

The filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_v h_u=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ and the $O(\sigma^2)$ part of $\langle u_kv_k\rangle$ can be absorbed in the effective $\phi$. In the strict steady-state $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ limit the time constants $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless ratio. The unresolved notational point is the inessential $+1$ absorbed in $S$ versus kept explicit in the definition of $c_{kl}$, which interchanges $-\rho/\phi\mu$ and $1+\rho/\phi\mu$.

Current round 4: Majority Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 converge on the dimensionless offset $\kappa_{0}=-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $\kappa_{*}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ in the excess-correlation convention, with $\tau_v,\tau_u$ absorbed in $\phi$. Minority Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 persist on the un-normalised product $\kappa=(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ and related additive $(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ forms, arguing multiplicative contribution of the two accumulators. The product argument is based on direct substitution before normalisation and is inconsistent with the stated steady-state assumption $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum s w x$ where $\tau_v,\tau_u$ disappear. Dimensional analysis favours the dimensionless ratio. The discussion remains split on notation $+1$ but not on the physical content $|\rho|/\phi\mu$.}

PRIVATE REFLECTION: {The mean-field $w$ nullcline is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$.
In the strict stationary limit used in the statement $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$, $s_{kk}=1$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$. With the uniform ansatz $w_l=w$, $\mu_l=\mu$ and the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2c_{kl}$,

dimensionless homeostatic-to-Hebbian ratio. For the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, $\kappa_0=|\rho|/\phi\mu>0$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_0$ for $S\to\infty$. 12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mean-field $w$ nullcline on the $w$ time scale is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$. With the uniform ansatz $w_l=w,\;\mu_l=\mu$ and, up to the inessential filter overlap ${\cal C}=\int h_vh_u$ which can be absorbed in an effective $\phi$,

$\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\;\langle u_k\rangle = w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl},\,s_{kk}=1$,

and with the $c_{kk}=1$ normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2c_{kl}$

$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\mu^2\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$.

Hence up to $w\mu$

$\phi\mu\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}+\rho\sum_l s_{kl}=0$,
$\displaystyle\frac{\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}}{\sum_l s_{kl}}=-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\equiv\kappa_0$.

On a translation invariant branch $S_k\equiv S$ and $c_{kl}=c$, $k\neq l$,

$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=s_{kk}c_{kk}+c\sum_{l\neq k}s_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$,

so

$\phi\mu\,[\,1+c(S-1)\,]+\rho S=0$,

$1+c(S-1)=\kappa_0 S$,

$c^{*}(S)=\dfrac{\kappa_0 S-1}{S-1}$,

with the $s$-weighted mean correlation at marginality

$\kappa_0=\langle c\rangle_s=S^{-1}\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=-\rho/\phi\mu=-\rho/\phi\langle x\rangle>0$ for the usual depressing sign $\rho<0$, i.e. in sign free form $|\kappa_0|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_0$.
The $\tau_v,\tau_u$ overlap ${\cal C}=(\tau_v+\tau_u)^{-1}$ merely renormalises the effective $\phi$; on the strict stationary limit $v_k=\phi x_k$, $u_k=\sum_l s_{kl}w_lx_l$ the dimensionless ratio $\rho/\phi\mu$ is $\tau_{v},\tau_{u}$ free.

In the excess-correlation convention $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=0$ the same zero drift is conventionally quoted as

$1+c^{*}(S-1)=\kappa_* S$,
$\kappa_*=1+\rho/\phi\mu=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$,
$\kappa_*-1=\rho/\phi\mu$,

so that $c^{*}=[\kappa_*S-1]/[S-1]$ and $c^{*}\to\kappa_*$ for $S\to\infty$. Up to the inessential additive unity $\kappa_*=1+\kappa_0$, $\kappa_0=-\rho/\phi\mu$ is the familiar homeostatic-to-Hebbian control parameter, often written sign free as $|\kappa|=|\rho|/\phi\mu$, with $\rho\to-\theta>0$ giving $\kappa_{+}=|\rho|/\phi\mu$.

Round 4 public positions: 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 reaffirm the dimensionless $-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ in the $1+$ convention, and stress that the filter overlap is absorbed in $\phi$ so $\tau_v,\tau_u$ drop out of the dimensionless mean field ratio. Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14,9 continue to advocate the product form $\kappa\propto(-\rho/\phi-\mu)\tau_u\tau_v$ or $(\rho/\phi-\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$, claiming multiplicative time constants from the sequential linear filters. That product is dimensionally inconsistent for a dimensionless correlation once ${\cal C}$ is absorbed in $\phi$, and corresponds to keeping the un-normalised kernel overlap explicit. No new algebraic evidence in round 4 changes the mean-field derivation; the disagreement remains the sign/additive-unity convention versus the un-normalised $\tau_u\tau_v$ product. Unresolved is only the conventional choice of $c_{kk}=1$ vs excess-correlation $c_{kk}=0$, i.e. whether $\kappa$ is quoted as $-\rho/\phi\mu$ or as $1+\rho/\phi\mu$, the two being related by the inessential $+1$.
